newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Q3 commission revs up on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Q3 commission revs up on fund sales.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co Inc said third quarter commission revenues rose by four percent to $860 million from $829 million a year ago, fueled by higher mutual fund sales and listed securities volume.
The firm said its principal transactions revenues soared 23 percent from a year ago to $818 million, with international trading revenues representing about 45 percent of the total.
Merrill Lynch reported higher third quarter and nine month revenues and earnings earlier Tuesday.
Merrill said third quarter investment banking revenues rose 33 percent to $471 million from $354 million due to increased equity and debt underwriting volumes.
Strategic service fees reached record levels, benefitting from gains in market share for global mergers and acquisitions completed during the quarter, the firm said.

Merrill said asset management and portfolio service fees reached a record $570 million, up 18 percent from $484 million posted in the 1995 third quarter due to continued growth in its asset management and other fee-based businesses. Assets under management were $213 billion at quarter-end, up 12 percent from last year.

The assets under management totals refer to those managed by Merrill Lynch Asset Management. Total assets in worldwide Private Client accounts reached a record $779 billion at the end of the 1996 third quarter, up $76 billion from last year.

Merrill said third quarter non-interest expenses increased 17 percent from the 1995 third quarter to $2.57 billion. The largest expense category, compensation and benefits, was up 16 percent to $1.61 billion due to higher incentive compensation related to improved profitability and increased headcount.
Compensation and benefits expense as a percentage of net revenues was 52.1 percent, compared with 51.9 percent in 1995's third quarter.

"The strength and diversity of Merrill Lynch's businesses allowed us to achieve another strong quarter as we continued to build our presence outside the United States," said chairman and chief executive Daniel Tully.
"For the sixth consecutive quarter our return on common equity exceeded 20 percent, reflecting our continued commitment to building shareholder value."
